title: Zigzag Grid Traversal With Skip
statement:
`grid` is a rectangular matrix of positive integers. Walk through it in snake order: row 0 from left to right, row 1 from right to left, row 2 from left to right again, and so on until every row is done.

Along this walk, keep the first cell, skip the next, keep the one after, and so on; the alternation carries on across row boundaries rather than restarting on each row. Return the values of the kept cells in the order the walk reaches them.
constraints: Every row of grid has the same length
notes:
## Intuition

The walk is a fixed order of all cells, so the task is careful bookkeeping. You could write out the whole snake walk and then keep its even positions; the reference does both at once, with a flag that flips after every visited cell.

The only real subtlety is that the alternation belongs to the walk, not to a row. When the rows have odd length, a row ends on a kept cell, so the next row begins with a skip.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `result` and `take = true`, because the first cell is kept.
2. For each `row`, count `step` from 0 to `cols - 1`. The column is `step` on even rows and `cols - 1 - step` on odd rows.
3. If `take` is set, push `grid[row][col]`.
4. Flip `take` after every cell, row ends included.
5. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]`. Row 0 runs left to right: `1` is kept and `take` flips to false, so `2` is skipped. Row 1 runs right to left, starting at column 1: `take` is true again, so `4` is kept and `3` is skipped. The result is `[1, 4]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): every cell is visited once.
- Space: O(m · n) for the output, which holds about half the cells; O(1) besides.

## Pitfalls

- Do not restart the pattern on each row. In a 3-column grid, row 1 starts with a skip (Example 3 keeps only the 5 from `[6, 5, 4]`).
- On odd rows the walk starts at the last column, so the first cell considered there is `grid[row][cols - 1]`.
- Keeping `col % 2 === 0` on every row is wrong: the kept cells are exactly those with `row + col` even, so odd rows keep their odd columns, listed right to left.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | values kept so far, in walk order |
| `take` | whether the next visited cell is kept |
| `row` | current row index |
| `cols` | number of columns |
| `step` | position of the cell within this row's walk |
| `col` | column of the cell at this step |

narration.2: result collects the kept values in the order the walk reaches them.
narration.3: The very first cell of the walk is kept.
narration.4: Visit the rows from top to bottom.
narration.6: step counts the cells of this row in walking order.
narration.7: Even rows run left to right and odd rows right to left, so the column depends on the row's parity.
narration.8: Is this cell one of the kept ones?
narration.11: Every visited cell flips the flag, so kept and skipped cells alternate along the whole walk, across rows too.
narration.14: All rows are done; return the kept values.
